Formulation  
Patient with a history of childhood asthma and atopic conditions now experiencing an acute exacerbation likely triggered by viral infection or allergen exposure (hay fever). Symptoms limit physical activity and speech. Good insight enables engagement with treatment. Protective social support present. No evidence of mental health disorder or acute safety concerns. Requires close follow-up to prevent deterioration.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Asthma Exacerbation  
- Patient Goal(s): Improve breathing and return to normal physical activity and work attendance  
- Clinical Goal(s): Resolve wheezing and shortness of breath; prevent complications; optimize asthma control  
- Actions (Patient):  
  • Use salbutamol inhaler regularly as advised (2-4 puffs every 4 hours initially)  
  • Obtain and use peak flow meter as instructed  
  • Record peak flow values morning and evening for one week  
  • Start regular antihistamines for hay fever symptoms  
  • Contact clinician promptly if fever or wheezing worsens  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  • Prescribe peak flow meter and spacer device with instructions for use  
  • Provide guidance on inhaler use frequency  
  • Recommend antihistamines for allergy control  
  • Review patient in one week, with phone consultation to discuss peak flow readings and consider further medication adjustments  

Secondary Problem: Allergic Rhinitis (Hay Fever)  
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce allergy symptoms contributing to asthma flare  
- Clinical Goal(s): Control hay fever symptoms to minimize asthma exacerbations  
- Actions (Patient): Obtain and take regular antihistamines as recommended  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Document allergy treatment recommendation; monitor symptom response at asthma review  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Asthma flare management, inhaler use, spacer device, peak flow monitoring, allergy control, when to seek immediate help  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased wheezing, persistent fever, difficulty completing sentences, reduced peak flow readings  
- Coping Strategies: Adherence to inhaler regimen, use of peak flow meter for self-monitoring, prompt contact with healthcare if symptoms deteriorate
